facts.statement: Intiornis is known from a partial hind limb discovered in the Las Curtiembres Formation.
facts.quote: The genus is known from a partial hind limb found in beds of the Upper Cretaceous Las Curtiembres Formation.

facts.statement: The genus was named by Fernando Emilio Novas, Federico Lisandro Agnolín, and Carlos Agustín Scanferla in 2010.
facts.quote: It was named by Fernando Emilio Novas, Federico Lisandro Agnolín and Carlos Agustín Scanferla in 2010

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Intiornis inexpectatus.
facts.quote: the type species is Intiornis inexpectatus

facts.statement: Intiornis had a body length of around 15 cm, roughly the size of a sparrow.
facts.quote: With the body length of around 15 cm Intiornis was the size of a sparrow

facts.statement: Intiornis possessed three primary toes on its limbs that were nearly the same length.
facts.quote: Three primary toes on a limb of Intiornis are nearly the same length

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that Intiornis's long, equal-length toes and large curved claws indicate an adaptation for perching.
facts.quote: Long toes of equal length and large curved claws suggest adaptability for perching.

facts.statement: Intiornis belongs to the family Avisauridae.
Intiornis is a member of the subclass Enantiornithes.
Intiornis is a monotypic genus known only from the species I. inexpectatus.
facts.quote: Es un género monotípico conocido a partir de la especie I. inexpectatus.

facts.statement: Intiornis lived between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Intiornis represents the smallest known enantiornithes from South America.
facts.quote: thus representing the smallest enantiornithes known from South America
